issues.legal_issue: A transfer made before a religious dedication can place the transferee in a position to dedicate the property and become its shebait.
material_facts: The founder purchased the property, built a temple on it, and installed the idol.
She executed a deed transferring the property to her nephew before any dedication had taken place.
The nephew thereafter managed the property and arranged for worship, and his successors continued that management.
issues.conclusion: The deed transferred the property before it had been dedicated; the donee’s subsequent acts made it Devottar property and constituted him the deity’s shebait, a position that passed to his heirs.
issues.legal_principle: Where the evidence establishes that property had not been dedicated before its transfer, the transfer may pass the property to the donee, whose subsequent acts may dedicate it and establish his shebaitship. The Court relied on the deed and the parties’ acts; it cited no statutory provision or earlier case for this conclusion.

predicates.property_not_previously_dedicated: The property had not been dedicated to the religious purpose before it was transferred.
predicates.transfer_preceded_dedication: The transfer occurred before the property was dedicated.
predicates.transferee_managed_temple_as_shebait: The transferee managed the temple and arranged for worship in the capacity of its shebait.
predicates.transferee_becomes_shebait: The transferee becomes the shebait of the deity.

issues.definition: When property is transferred before dedication and the transferee thereafter manages the temple as shebait, the transferee becomes the shebait.

issues.legal_issue: A person who performs worship and manages temple property with the shebait’s permission does not thereby acquire the office of shebait.
material_facts: The successive holders of the estate appointed priests and arranged for worship at the temple.
A priest acknowledged that he lived in the temple with permission and held the deity’s ornaments on behalf of the estate holder, undertaking to return them on demand.
The priest’s descendants and their widows performed worship and took part in temple management, but the evidence did not show that they had asserted shebaitship before the widow’s will.
The widow’s performance of temple duties and payments to temple officers were consistent with her acting for the shebait.
issues.conclusion: The estate holder and his successor were the shebaits; the widow was only a pujari and did not acquire shebaitship through her performance of worship or management of the property.
issues.legal_principle: The character of a person’s role in temple management is determined from the documentary evidence and the parties’ acts. Performing worship or exercising control under the shebait’s permission does not, without evidence of an independent claim to the office, establish shebaitship. No statutory provision or earlier case was cited for this conclusion.

predicates.temple_management_dispute: The proceeding concerns a dispute over who holds the shebaitship of a temple.
predicates.worshipper_performed_duties_under_shebai: The worshipper performed worship or managed temple affairs under the authority or permission of the shebait.
predicates.records_show_shebait_retained_management: Documents or other evidence show that the shebait retained responsibility for temple management and treated the worshipper as acting on his behalf.
predicates.worshipper_is_only_pujari: The worshipper holds the role of pujari rather than the office of shebait.

issues.definition: When a temple dispute concerns a worshipper who performed duties under the shebait’s authority and the records show that the shebait retained management, the worshipper is only a pujari.

issues.legal_issue: Possession held in the capacity of a pujari or agent, without a clear hostile assertion of shebaitship, does not bar a claim to the shebaitship by limitation.
material_facts: The widow performed worship and managed temple affairs in a role consistent with that of a pujari acting for the shebait.
The evidence did not establish that she had clearly asserted a right to shebaitship before making a will claiming an interest in the property.
The suit sought possession of temple property and recognition of the claimant’s shebaitship.
issues.conclusion: The claim was not barred by limitation, and the defence that the widow had acquired shebaitship by adverse possession was rejected.
issues.legal_principle: Possession in a subordinate or representative capacity, without a clear hostile assertion of the claimed right, does not establish adverse possession that bars the claim. The Court cited no statutory provision or earlier case in rejecting the limitation defence.

predicates.suit_concerns_recovery_of_temple_propert: The proceeding seeks recovery of temple property or recognition of the right to shebaitship.
predicates.possession_was_as_pujari_or_agent: The person in possession performed temple duties as a pujari or agent for the shebait.
predicates.clear_hostile_claim_of_shebaitship: The person in possession clearly asserted a claim to shebaitship hostile to the claimant’s right.
predicates.claim_not_barred_by_limitation: The claim is not barred by limitation.

issues.definition: A claim to temple property or shebaitship is not barred when possession was held as a pujari or agent and no clear hostile claim to shebaitship was made.
